paper.title: Better Algorithms for Stochastic Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions

unmapped: Adaptive adversary corrupts rewards after observing the stochastic draws; corruption C = sum_t ||R~^t - R^t||_inf is a random variable and unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: A stochastic reward $\rew^t_i \in [0,1]$ is drawn for each arm $i$ from its reward distribution; The adversary observes the vector $\rew^t$ and generates corrupted rewards $\wt{\rew}^t \in [0,1]^K$; The player picks $i_t \in [K]$ ... we measure the level of corruption $C$ as: $C = \sum_{t=1}^T \norm{\wt{\rew}^t - \rew^t}_\infty$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with adversarial corruptions, known maximal reward
settings.definition_quote: Finally, consider the case where the player knows the value of $\mu^\star$.

extra_assumptions: C is the realized (random) corruption level, unknown to the learner

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \cref{alg:barbar} is bounded by \[ O\Bigg(KC + \sum_{i \neq i^\star} \frac{\log{T}}{\Delta_i} \log\!\Big(\frac{K}{\delta}\log{T}\Big) \!\Bigg). \]

results.notes: Algorithm takes T and delta as parameters; agnostic to C.

source.quote: To convert the bound of \cref{thm:main} into a bound on the expected regret of the algorithm, one can set $\delta = 1 / T$ ... Thus, the expected regret is bounded by $O(K\,\Ex[C] + \sum_{i \neq i^\star} \frac{1}{\Delta_i} \log^2(KT))$.

results.notes: Corollary stated in prose, not a formal theorem.

bound.regime: C <= T/2; holds even for known C; K = 2 instance

source.quote: We show an $\Omega(C)$ lower bound for the pseudo-regret of any algorithm. ... for the pseudo-regret under this contamination model there is a lower bound of $\Omega(C)$ that holds for all $C$ up to $T \div 2$. Moreover this lower bound holds even for the case of known $C$.

results.notes: Informal argument; 'with constant probability' regret Omega(C); recorded as expectation-level.

source.label: lem:deltaji_lb_changed
source.quote: Hence, if we know $\mu^\star$, the total regret is at most $ O(C) + \wt{O}\big( \!\sum_{i \neq i^\star}\! 1\div\Delta_i \big). $

results.notes: Proof sketch in prose; holds on event E (prob >= 1-delta). C term is O(C) without logs, Õ applies to the sum term.
